preamble: Retroflexion of the dental/alveolar voiced stop [d] to [ɖ]. In Indo-Aryan it occurs by assimilation to a preceding retroflex (Sanskrit nīḍa 'nest' < *niẓḍás) and word-initially in a set of lexemes in Middle Indo-Aryan (Sanskrit dáśati 'bites' > Prakrit ḍasaï > Hindi ḍasnā).

examples.to: Prakrit ḍasaï > Hindi डसना ḍasnā /ɖəsnɑː/ 'to bite (of a snake), sting'
examples.note: Unconditioned initial retroflexion of dental d in Middle Indo-Aryan.
Prakrit 𑀤𑁄𑀮𑀇 still has the dental.
The d became retroflex by assimilation to the preceding RUKI-retroflexed sibilant *ẓ, which was then lost with compensatory lengthening; cognate with Latin nīdus, English nest.
Same development of *žd to ḍ with loss of the sibilant and compensatory lengthening.
